systems.name: creative-apps
systems.description: The macOS app shells of the creative suite: five SwiftUI apps (Flare, Design, Photo, Library, Halo), each over a Linux-safe Model target, plus the SuiteUI design system.

containers.name: SuiteUI
containers.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): tokens, Liquid Glass primitives, the SuiteWindow shell, toolbar palette, sidebar rows and sections, content-layer surfaces, pro inspector rows and scrub fields, a thumbnail grid and a timeline strip. macOS only; knows no Model or engine.

components.name: SuiteUI sources
components.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): spacing, radius, size, type and color tokens; Liquid Glass applied in one snapshot-aware place (Glass) and GlassPanel; the SuiteWindow shell (sidebar, content, inspector) with SidebarSection and SidebarRow; ToolbarGroup palette actions; the content layer (CanvasSurface, SurfaceCard, EmptyStateView, ViewerStatusBar); the editor shell after the Ripple editor (EditorShell, EditorTopBar and its bar items, the docked ToolbarGroup rail, CanvasViewport with its Ruler, optional checkerboard, ZoomMath clamped zoom and fit, and CanvasMarks, SegmentedTabs and the ColorWell hex row); pro inspector parts (InspectorHeader, InspectorRows, ScrubField and NumericInput number entry); the Studio easing parts (CurveEditor, StudioScrubRow, ChoiceChips); ThumbnailGrid with its selection math; and TimelineStrip with its frame mapping, shared by Flare and Halo.

containers.name: FlareApp
containers.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/FlareApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads FlareModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: FlareApp sources
components.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene, its menu bar (FlareCommands) and views in Sources/FlareApp, including the easing inspector on the live FlareWorkspace, built from SuiteUI, and PlaybackDriver, which feeds NSScreen display-link target timestamps into the workspace's play clock, and StagePath, which turns FlareCore paths and colors into CGPath (one addCurve per cubic) and sRGB CGColor for the stage, and FlareAutosave, which writes the dirty document's RecoveryFile atomically off the main actor once autosave is due and removes it after a save, and on launch reads and decodes it off the main thread into a RecoveryOffer to restore or discard.

containers.name: FlareModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window. FlareWorkspace: the open FlareCore document, selected scene and drawing tool. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: FlareModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window: FlareWorkspace (document, selection, tool, frame and playback, drafts) and FlareServices: the use-case contracts, their live conformances over FlareCore, and the fixture fakes the UI track and snapshots run on. FlareWorkspaceState holds the export, assist and file-load states the workspace stores. FlareFiles opens .flare files through load (progress first, a pure decode the app runs off the main thread, then the landing), hands the app a save's bytes, and keeps the file name, the window title and the dirty flag (the document against the one last opened or saved), with section 3.3's alert text for each FormatError, the Open Recent list (file paths, most recent first, at most ten), and the autosave due time (30 seconds after the last edit, only while dirty) with the recovery bytes of the dirty document, and restoring a recovered document as unsaved, untitled work. FlareSelection picks layers or items by click, Shift-click and marquee, and gives the selection box's bounds; FlareDrag turns stage gestures into a draft or move preview and commits each once, on mouse-up, as one named undo step; FlareDrawing adds the Ellipse tool's draft and its one-step commit; FlareScenes adds, renames, removes (never the last), reorders and sets up scenes; FlareGuides adds, moves (one coalesced step per drag), removes and clears ruler guides; FlareEdit runs the Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Select All, Deselect), each one named undo step or disabled with the reason it refuses with; FlareAnimate holds auto-key and the inspector's animated properties (Mixed across layers, one coalesced step per scrub, the stopwatch and keyframe button); EasingEditing is the easing editor's contract, which FlareWorkspace conforms to over FlareCore's SetKeyframeEasing, with FakeEasingEditing as its in-memory stand-in for UI work. FlareOnionState holds onion skin and motion path preferences and reads ghosts and the path from services.onion. FlareServices holds one fake per use-case contract (FakeScenes, FakeStage, FakeHits, FakeShapes, FakeProperties with section 2's not-animated rule, FakeKeyframes, FakeEasing, FakeOnion, FakeLibrary, FakeMachines, FakePreview and FakeExport with FakeRasterizer so far, NotBuilt for the rest) over the fixture documents in FlareFixtures (empty, bounce, character, button, button with states, button with machine and showcase). ExportScan names everything an export can't write (text, symbol animation, machines, Lottie's background); FlareExport holds the export sheet's options, warnings and run. FlareSymbols holds the Library tab's symbols and swatches, Convert to Symbol, place, the reason Delete is disabled while a symbol is in use, and editing a symbol in place: the owner switch, the symbol's length on the timeline and the scene frame to return to. FlarePlaybackTicks is the playback driver's platform-neutral core: PlaybackTicker turns display-link target timestamps into the elapsed seconds the play clock advances by, FlareWorkspace.tick is the link's entry point, and PlaybackBudget holds QB-L4's dropped-frame gate. MachineLayout lays out a state machine's graph for the Interactions editor: columns by breadth-first distance from the initial state, unreachable states in a last column. FlareMachines holds the Interactions editor's state: the edited machine, states from frame labels, transitions and inputs, each edit one named undo step through services.machines with refusals in machineError, and the live preview over services.preview, which any machine edit stops.

containers.name: DesignApp
containers.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell. Reads DesignModel and sends it intents through DesignWindow; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: DesignApp sources
components.description: The Design app (vector and UI design): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/DesignApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell: the window and its intents (DesignWindow, DesignIntent), the top bar, the tool rail, the canvas with selection handles (drawn above the page clip) and the inline text editor, the Properties | Layers panel (a List of the pages and the layer tree, and the inspector's Align row in DesignAlignBar), the File, Edit, Page, Object (Align) and View menus, and the open and save panels.

containers.name: DesignModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: pages, the node tree on each page (with fills and text) and which Layers rows are expanded, the selection, the tool, the model-owned undo history, the canvas gestures and the file codec. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: DesignModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: DesignWorkspace (pages, the selected page and node, the tool, the open file's URL), the multi-layer selection (DesignSelection: the ordered selected layers with the last as primary, Shift-click toggling, the box around them), DesignNode (the node tree on a page, each node with a fill and text, in absolute page points) and the tree flattened into rows under the expanded set, DesignHistory (the model-owned undo and redo, one named step per edit; New File's step carries the replaced document's file URL, which Undo puts back), the canvas gestures (hit testing, the handles a selection shows, draw, move, resize, nudge, delete, in DesignCanvasEditing and DesignDrawing), the inline text edit (DesignText), the inspector's header lines (DesignInspectorContent), the lock that covers a node's subtree and the line saying why (DesignLocking), the Layers row's eye and lock toggles and the hidden-in-tree check (DesignLayerToggles), the held-id index id minting reads (DesignHeldIDs), aligning the selected layer to its enclosing frame or page with the reason a command is off (DesignAlign), and the file codec (DesignFile).

containers.name: PhotoApp
containers.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads PhotoModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: PhotoApp sources
components.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI's EditorShell: the window and its intents, the top bar, tool rail and canvas, the Adjust | Layers panel (tool options, adjustment sections with the Levels gamma ScrubField and the Curves tone curve over its histogram, the layer list), the export, image size and straighten sheets (the straighten preview turns the canvas picture on the GPU under a grid), the File, Edit (Undo, Redo, and Cut, Copy and Paste on the image unless a text field has focus or a sheet is up), Select, Image, Layer and View menus, the general pasteboard read and written as PNG and TIFF (PhotoPasteboard) and watched for the Edit menu, the coalescing canvas renderer, the stroke pacer that applies a display frame's drag samples at once, the pen pressure and the Option key read from AppKit for canvas drags, the window's autosave to a recovery file and its restore offer at launch (PhotoAutosave), the app delegate (Finder opens, and the unsaved-changes prompt on Quit) and the window's close guard that asks before a dirty window closes, and the ImageIO codec behind PhotoModel's PhotoImageCodec.

containers.name: PhotoModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: the canvas as a CoreRaster PixelBuffer, its layer stack, selected layer and tool, adjustment settings, and inspector and Layer menu state. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: PhotoModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: PhotoWorkspace (the open image's size and name, the layer stack with each layer's offset and its pixels as copy-on-write CoreRaster tiles (TiledPixels), so an edit copies only the tiles it touches, the selected layer, tool, and the brush's and eraser's own tool options with the brush cursor diameter, the marquee selection and pending crop), the tools' drags (brush and eraser dabs, marquee, crop, move, and the Clone and Heal tools' Option-click to sample and drag to clone or heal), the clone stamp (a sampled source and a stroke that copies from it at a fixed offset onto the selected layer, and heal, the same stroke with each dab shifted to the tone where it lands), selection edits and crop, Image Size, Rotate and Straighten (worked out off the main actor, committed unless the image changed), the undo history (the tiles an edit changed, layer lists and whole stacks, read as a list of named steps from "New Image" or "Open" with a jump to any step), the tile-parallel renderer with damage tracking (a full frame as the reference, or the live canvas's update: only the damaged tiles, premultiplied) and the adjustments it applies (exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, blur) with the curve editor's samples and histogram, opening and exporting through the PhotoImageCodec protocol, the adjustment settings and logarithmic gamma track (with the Gamma field's commit, a no-op for the value it shows), what the inspector shows (with the panel header lines and the viewer status size text), and when each Layer menu item can run (with Bring Forward and Send Backward, one place up or down the stack, and Select Layer Above and Below), and the live edit services (the clipboard and layer merging, through the renderer's per-layer composite) behind Cut, Copy and Paste of pixels (a pasted layer, or a new image with none open) and Duplicate Layer, Merge Down and Flatten Image, each one named undo step with its reason when it can't run.

containers.name: LibraryApp
containers.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads LibraryModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: LibraryApp sources
components.description: The Library app (photo catalog): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/LibraryApp, built from SuiteUI: the window with its thumbnail grid, the loupe (one photo fitted in CanvasSurface with its position readout, arrow keys and Escape), the metadata inspector for the selected photos (rating, flag, color label), and the File > Load Sample Photos, View > Grid and Loupe, View > Sort By and thumbnail size commands.

containers.name: LibraryModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: the catalog's photos, sidebar collections with counts, the selected collection and sort order, and seeded sample photos. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: LibraryModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Library's window: LibraryCatalog (photos, collections with counts, the selected collection, sort order, the loupe's photo, stepping and position), PhotoItem with its sort orders, metadata edits on the selected photos with mixed values (PhotoMetadata, PhotoFlag) and the metadata inspector's accessibility identifiers (MetadataInspectorID), and 60 seeded sample photos.

containers.name: HaloApp
containers.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads HaloModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: HaloApp sources
components.description: The Halo app (motion graphics): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/HaloApp, built from SuiteUI: the window, the Layer and Composition menus, the composition inspector (Pro density header, Composition rows and layer list), the viewer's status bar and timeline strip (scrub, select a layer, I and O set in and out points), the New Composition sheet, the alert for a refused rename, and the hidden readouts the UI journeys read where XCUITest reads a value empty (#262).

containers.name: HaloModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: the project's compositions and their layers, the selected composition, New Composition settings, and refused renames. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: HaloModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Halo's window: HaloProject (compositions, the selected one, unique names), HaloTimeline (each composition's playhead, timecodes, the layers active at a frame, the strip's rows, in and out points at the playhead), HaloLayer (kind, span, color, opacity, CoreRaster blend mode, solid rectangle), FrameRenderer (composites a composition's solids into one preview frame with CoreRaster), HaloStatusText (the inspector header, Composition rows and status-bar timecode text), the New Composition draft and its validated settings, and RefusedRename, which keeps a refused composition rename for the alert.

containers.name: SuiteModel
containers.description: Linux-safe values, contracts, fakes and pure logic shared by every app and the launcher. Foundation only; imports no app Model and no engine.

components.name: Identity and type registry
components.description: SuiteApp (the five apps and the launcher), bundle ids under one prefix (SuiteIdentity.prefix), and SuiteTypeRegistry: every document and pasteboard type each app reads and writes and the default app per type. Bundle/Info/*.plist mirror it; a test checks both.

components.name: Suite store
components.description: SuiteLocations (the support folder, -SuiteSupportDir override) and FileStore: revisioned JSON files written by atomic replace under an exclusive lock file, merged with the caller's pure merge.

components.name: Contracts
components.description: One protocol per suite use case (blueprint section 5): switching, recents, new documents, routing, hand-offs, round trip, pasteboard, assets, links, animation import, preferences, settings route, onboarding, updates, thumbnails, home, and SuiteDocumentHost, which each app Model conforms to so it can act on hand-offs.

components.name: Fakes and fixtures
components.description: A fake per contract with an unavailable reason, and SuiteFixtures: the journeys' store contents, written into the live store by the launcher.

components.name: Services
components.description: SuiteServices: one member per contract, .fake and the slots SuiteShell fills for .live.

components.name: Recents
components.description: RecentsList: merge, dedupe by file identity, cap 200, filter by app, search; the rules for when an app records.

components.name: Routing
components.description: Which app opens a type, the Open In list for a document, and Finder routing decisions for the launcher.

components.name: Hand-offs
components.description: HandOff values (verb, payload, return address), the versioned codec and the lifecycle (pending, accepted, returned, cancelled, expired).

components.name: Switching
components.description: Switch requests and receipts, run states, the Switch To menu model.

components.name: Home state
components.description: Home sections (new tiles and presets, recents grid, running apps strip), search and filter, HomeLayout column math, and HomeModel, the home window's observable view-model.

components.name: Pasteboard coding
components.description: SuiteClipItem and its typed representations (suite asset envelope, SVG, PNG, colour, text); best-item choice for a target app.

components.name: Round trip
components.description: Library to Photo to Library edit sessions and their states.

components.name: Assets
components.description: SuiteAsset, SuiteSwatch, the asset index: add, update with a new revision, remove, search.

components.name: Links
components.description: AssetLink and its status (current, update available, missing) for placed assets.

components.name: Animation import
components.description: AnimationSummary of a .flare file (size, rate, length, scenes) for Halo's Open In.

components.name: Preferences
components.description: SuitePreferences (General and a pane per app), defaults, change records.

components.name: Onboarding
components.description: Onboarding pages, the person's choices, and when to show them.

components.name: Updates
components.description: Update feed parsing, version comparison, the offer and the install plan.

components.name: Packaging
components.description: BundleLayout (where each executable and framework sits, run paths), SizeReport and SizeBudget with evaluate.

containers.name: SuiteShell
containers.description: macOS glue every app process links: live conformances needing AppKit or Launch Services, shared menu commands, the adoption modifier.

components.name: Live services
components.description: SuiteServices.live and one slot file per member; each feature swaps only its own slot.

components.name: App launching and Switch To
components.description: Open or activate an embedded app (NSWorkspace.openApplication, NSRunningApplication.activate), run states, the Switch To commands.

components.name: Hand-off transport
components.description: Writes a hand-off file and opens it with the target app; receives one through onOpenURL.

components.name: Store watcher
components.description: Posts and observes the org.creativesuite.suite.changed distributed notification.

components.name: Pasteboard and drag bridges
components.description: Maps SuiteClipItem to NSPasteboard items and drag item providers and back.

components.name: Documents bridge
components.description: Records opens and saves in recents, writes thumbnails, builds the Open In submenu.

components.name: Adoption modifier
components.description: The .suiteApp(_:host:) modifier each app adds to its scene, SuiteAppDelegate (receives hand-off files through application(_:open:) and passes them to the app's SuiteDocumentHost), and the settings route to the launcher.

containers.name: AfterGlowApp
containers.description: The launcher executable inside AfterGlow.app: home, assets page, settings, onboarding, updater, file router.

components.name: Launcher scene and router
components.description: @main AfterGlowApp: the home Window, the Settings scene, the onboarding window, and the router that forwards opened documents to the embedded app. Hand-off verbs the launcher acts on (open settings, routed files) are LauncherRouter+<Area>.swift extensions, one per feature.

components.name: Home window
components.description: New tiles and presets, recents grid with search and app filter, running apps strip.

components.name: Assets page
components.description: The shared asset and colour library in the home sidebar.

components.name: Settings
components.description: One Settings window: General and one pane per app.

components.name: Onboarding
components.description: Three first-launch pages.

components.name: Updater
components.description: Check, offer sheet, progress, install and relaunch.

containers.name: AfterGlow bundle
containers.description: The packaged artifact's inputs: Info.plists with document and exported types, icons, the engine re-export file, the release graph in project.yml, scripts/bundle-apps and scripts/size-report (protected: supervisor merges).

components.name: Bundle inputs
components.description: Info.plists per bundle, icons, entitlements, and Bundle/Engines/CreativeEngines.swift (re-exports FlareCore, CoreRaster, CoreColor for the one shared engine framework).

containers.name: SuiteModelTests
containers.description: Model tests, contract conformance suites, model budgets, BuildGraphTests (Package.swift vs project.yml) and the registry-vs-plist check.

components.name: SuiteModelTests sources
components.description: as the container

containers.name: AfterGlow journeys
containers.description: XCUITest bundle AfterGlowJourneyTests: drives the launcher and the apps through it; every shot audited.

components.name: AfterGlow journey files
components.description: as the container

systems.name: creative-core
systems.description: The pure-Swift engines the Models call (github.com/qbtrix/creative-core), pinned to one commit (revision: in Package.swift, recorded in the committed Package.resolved) and moved only by a bump PR from scripts/bump-core.

containers.name: FlareCore library
containers.description: Animation document model, commands with undo, timeline, file format and export.

containers.name: CoreColor library
containers.description: Color spaces and conversions.

containers.name: CoreRaster library
containers.description: Pixel buffers, compositing and image operations.
